purpose: Forced-removal rule: a leave_intent's subject (payload.pubkey, self-declared in the message BODY) may only enqueue a removal for the group member matching its own AUTHENTICATED sender (the S1 seam's AuthenticatedSender). A leave_intent naming a different subject than its sender is dropped at the handler boundary before enqueueLeave — no removal enqueued, no departure rendered. Readiness-only per AC-MV-1: under the app-layer-only stub the attacker controls both payload.pubkey and sender.pubkey, so this does not yet stop a real forced removal; it becomes load-bearing once the out-of-scope MLS backbone feeds a true authenticated sender.

public_api.name: createLeaveIntentHandler
public_api.description: Unchanged public surface (pre-existing from S1/S2). Internal handleLeaveIntent now gates deps.enqueueLeave on payload.pubkey === sender.pubkey.toLowerCase() before calling it.

public_api.name: parseLeaveIntent
public_api.description: Unchanged wire shape ({ pubkey: string } JSON). The returned pubkey is now canonicalized to lowercase hex so the handler's subject===sender comparison is a like-for-like string compare against AuthenticatedSender.pubkey.

dependencies_allowed: app/src/lib/marmot/applicationRumorDispatcher.ts (AuthenticatedSender, ApplicationRumor, DispatcherContext, RumorHandler types — S1 seam, pre-existing)
dependencies_forbidden: no change to MarmotContext.tsx fireAutoCommit / commit-time re-verification (explicitly out of scope per spec.md Non-Goals — the enqueue-time gate is this story's rule)
no change to the dispatcher choke-point drop (S1's scope, already lands sender.pubkey === rumor.pubkey before fan-out)
